In this case, the 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm likely affects the ulnar nerve, which runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. The ulnar nerve is responsible for sensory innervation to the palmar surface of the little finger. Therefore, loss of sensation over the palmar surface of the little finger is the most likely outcome. The reasoning aligns with standard medical consensus regarding the anatomy and function of the ulnar nerve in the forearm and hand.
